purpose: Frozen blind set measured once per system, never used for tuning. Scope: source-heldout (FT answer passages excluded), not unseen-evidence (FT context overlap allowed). Curated from the frozen corpus without running any retriever or model.

cases.query: What is the 'rented suit' story Buffett tells about insurance accounting, and what lesson does he draw from it for his own reporting?

gold_claims.claim: A man abroad asked his sister to handle his father's funeral and kept receiving a $15 bill because the father had been buried in a rented suit.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1984 letter; unit=dollars per monthly bill; definition=the recurring charge revealed by the punchline of the funeral story.

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire has tried to include all of its 'rented suit' liabilities in its current financial statement, but its record of past error should make it humble and readers suspicious.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1984 letter; unit=qualitative accounting caution; definition=applying the story to insurance liabilities and past reserving error.

gold_claims.claim: Buffett says he will continue to report the errors, plus or minus, that surface each year.
gold_claims.verification_note: 1984 letter; unit=qualitative reporting commitment; definition=annual disclosure of reserve errors.

cases.verification_note: 1984_p0081 tells the rented-suit story and 1984_p0082 applies it to Berkshire's liability reporting and error disclosure.
